info.title: DND Campaign Vault Server API
info.description:
Comprehensive OpenAPI documentation for the DND Campaign Vault API.

Notes:
- Request/response envelopes follow `{ data, error }`.
- Operations may use the existing session cookie or a scoped bearer API key (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`).
- Bearer keys are subject to the owner's current campaign access and the key's resource permissions.
- The stateless MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint is available at `/mcp` on this same server; it exposes only the named operations documented in `docs/AgentIntegration.md`. The API remains the authorization and business-logic authority.

get.description: Auto-documented from server route `artifacts/[artifactId].get.ts`. This operation uses the project standard API envelope `{ data, error }`.

Streams a private artifact after read access is verified. Private recording and recap playback use the artifactId already included in their resource responses to request this stream directly; there is no private playback-URL lookup. Campaign media without read access returns 403, and a missing or deleted artifact returns 404. A storage adapter with range support serves one valid `Range` request as 206; otherwise the complete artifact is returned. Malformed or multiple ranges deliberately fall back to 200. Starts beyond the artifact, reversed ranges, zero-length suffixes, and unsafe integer values return 416. Oversized valid ends are clamped to the artifact size.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: One byte range for media seeking, for example `bytes=0-1023` or `bytes=-1024`. It is ignored when storage does not support range reads.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: When present, the response is sent with `Content-Disposition: attachment` so the browser saves the file instead of opening it.

200.description: Complete binary artifact with the artifact's stored MIME type. This is also returned for missing, malformed, or multiple Range values, and when storage cannot range-read.

Accept-Ranges.description: Present with `bytes` when the storage adapter supports range reads.

Content-Length.description: Present when the storage adapter reports the complete artifact size.

206.description: Requested single byte range as a binary artifact.

Content-Range.description: The byte interval served and the full artifact size.

Content-Length.description: The number of bytes in the partial response.

416.description: The requested byte range cannot be satisfied. The response is the standard JSON API error envelope, not an artifact stream.

Content-Range.description: The complete artifact size, expressed as an unsatisfied byte range.

get.description: Read current encounter state and role-aware availableActions. Selection is local UI state and does not change the turn.

200.description: Updated encounter state, including phase, participants, conditions, history, activeParticipantId, and availableActions with reasons.

patch.description: Update metadata in Planned/Active/Paused, or execute a typed lifecycle action. start: Planned with participants; pause: Active; resume: Paused with participants; complete: Active/Paused; abandon: Planned/Active/Paused; reopen: Completed/Abandoned to Paused, preserving state; reset: Active/Paused to Planned, resetting round/turn only. Raw status/currentRound/currentTurnIndex updates are rejected. Invalid phases return 409 ENCOUNTER_ACTION_UNAVAILABLE.

200.description: Updated encounter state, including phase, participants, conditions, history, activeParticipantId, and availableActions with reasons.

get.description: Auto-documented from server route `encounters/[encounterId]/combatants/index.get.ts`. This operation uses the project standard API envelope `{ data, error }`.

post.description: Creates a combatant, filling omitted HP, armorClass, and speed from its campaign-linked character sheet or saved stat block. Glossary sources use an unambiguous linked character sheet. Explicit values (including zero) win; saved stat-block values take precedence over character defaults. Explicit maxHp initializes omitted currentHp; otherwise source current HP or default max HP is used. Missing stats remain unset. Uses the standard API envelope `{ data, error }`. Planned/Active/Paused only. Batch {participants:[...]} accepts 1â€“50 entries atomically and returns full encounter state; legacy single input returns the created participant. No partial batch writes. Planned/Active/Paused only. Batch {participants:[...]} accepts 1â€“50 entries atomically and returns full encounter state; legacy single input returns the created participant. No partial batch writes.

200.description: Batch: full encounter state. Single input: created combatant in the standard envelope.

patch.description: Damage/healing requires Active/Paused and known current HP. Conditions may be prepared in Planned and edited in Active/Paused. All target ids must belong to the encounter; duplicate or invalid targets reject the whole batch. Numeric amounts are integers 1â€“9999. Finished encounters are read-only until reopened.

200.description: Updated encounter state, including phase, participants, conditions, history, activeParticipantId, and availableActions with reasons.

404.description: Encounter or target inaccessible; nothing changed.

post.summary: Call the stateless MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint
post.description: Send an MCP JSON-RPC request with a scoped bearer API key. Uses JSON responses and no server-side MCP session. An Origin header, when present, must match the configured public application origin. Campaign tool calls retain REST campaign and resource authorization. The dice_roll tool accepts a notation string (1-200 characters) and optional mode: normal (default), advantage, or disadvantage. Normal mode returns notation, mode, terms with individual dice and signed subtotals, and total. Advantage/disadvantage require a single d20 with an optional integer modifier (e.g. d20+5) and return notation, mode, both dice in rolls, selectedRoll, modifier, and total with the modifier applied once. It uses the shared dice roller and requires only a valid API key. Agents should prefer it over inventing roll results. Rolls are not persisted.

200.description: MCP JSON-RPC result or protocol error

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired, or revoked bearer key

406.description: Client must accept application/json and text/event-stream

500.description: MCP request could not be processed

AgentConditionCreateRequest.description: Exhaustion is case-insensitive and uses remaining as a level (1-6), with no duration or automatic ticking. Levels can be corrected in either direction and the condition can be removed; it cannot be renamed. The long-rest encounter effect removes one level.

AgentConditionUpdateRequest.description: Exhaustion is case-insensitive and uses remaining as a level (1-6), with no duration or automatic ticking. Levels can be corrected in either direction and the condition can be removed; it cannot be renamed. The long-rest encounter effect removes one level.

condition.description: For Exhaustion, remaining is the level (1-6, default 1) and duration is ignored. Duplicate exhaustion is rejected.

changes.description: For Exhaustion, remaining sets the level (1-6). Existing Exhaustion cannot be renamed.

oneOf.description: Confirms a proper long rest and removes one exhaustion level from each target in this encounter. Does not heal HP.

EncounterEffectRequest.description: Damage that drops a player character from positive HP to zero adds one exhaustion level, up to 6. Exhaustion is encounter-local; its remaining field stores the level, duration is null, and turn advancement never decrements it. long-rest removes one level; condition-update and condition-remove correct it directly. It cannot be renamed, and repeated condition-add is rejected.

activeParticipantId.description: Current turn participant in Active/Paused; null in other phases or when empty. UI selection is independent.

items.description: Participant id, source links, side, initiative, HP, AC, speed, flags, notes and timestamps.

floorCount.description: Total floor count, including a basement when enabled. Only BUILDING supports more than one floor.

buildingType.description: Room brief for building maps. Independent of the free-text theme, which only labels generated content. Other map types ignore it.

encounterFlow.description: Layout flow from an entrance through an objective to an exit. Changing this setting takes effect on generation; existing maps keep their geometry.

encounterScale.description: Encounter scope. SINGLE generates one objective fight while retaining separate entry, objective and exit spaces.

EncounterMapGeneratorConfig.description: Encounter map generation settings. Missing mapType and floorCount remain compatible with existing single-floor dungeons. Multi-floor buildings contain aligned stair connections.

floor.description: Zero-based floor; omitted values use the ground floor (0).

kind.description: Generated spatial role. Optional for legacy rooms.
Omitted legacy values represent a passage.

roomId.description: Geometry room ID. Owned features must fit inside that room on the same floor; unowned legacy terrain remains supported.

width.description: Stair footprint width in cells. Omitted legacy values use 1.

height.description: Stair footprint height in cells. Omitted legacy values use 1.

kind.description: Omitted legacy values represent stairs. Both kinds connect adjacent floors through a shared footprint.

EncounterMapStair.description: Aligned stair footprint inside both referenced rooms on adjacent floors. x and y identify its top-left cell. New building layouts use dedicated stairwell rooms; the complete footprint must remain inside both rooms.

floorLabels.description: Ordered labels for zero-based floors. When present, the number of labels must equal floorCount (or 1 for legacy maps).

EncounterMapData.description: Portable encounter map geometry and generated content. Legacy maps may omit mapType, floorCount and floor fields; these represent a single-floor dungeon. Terrain and stairs are optional for legacy maps. Portals, room kinds, stair dimensions and GM flow metadata are additive and optional for older maps. Imports validate portal geometry and flow references rather than accepting dangling routes.

floor.description: Zero-based floor; omitted legacy bounds use the ground floor (0).
Zero-based floor; omitted values use the ground floor (0).

EncounterMapGeometryPatchRequest.description: Ordered map edits. Rooms, walls and zones may target an existing floor. Corridors connect rooms on one floor. Stair-linked rooms cannot be deleted or moved/resized away from their complete stair footprint. Room, corridor and wall geometry edits clear generated flow metadata; zone edits preserve it. Moving/resizing a portal room reanchors its exterior route; removing the room removes its attached portals. Invalid final map geometry is rejected before persistence. Room-owned terrain moves with its room and is removed with it; resizing a room to clip owned terrain is rejected.

mapType.description: Current generated map type; legacy maps use DUNGEON.

floorCount.description: Current generated floor count; legacy maps use 1.

isSecret.description: Secret access points are omitted from player-safe views and exports even if their attached room is visible.

EncounterMapPortal.description: Orthogonal exterior route attached to an existing room. The first point is a wall cell inside that room and the last is on the map boundary (0 or width/height minus 1). Every point must remain inside the map. The room supplies the floor.

EncounterMapFlow.description: GM-only generated route. Entry, objective and exit reference three distinct visible rooms. The entry and exit must have matching nonsecret ENTRANCE and EXIT portals. The ordered route starts at entryRoomId, visits objectiveRoomId, and ends at exitRoomId; every room must exist and consecutive rooms must be joined by a corridor or stair. A route can revisit rooms, for example when returning from upper floors to a ground-floor exit. Geometry/topology edits clear this metadata. Player-safe projections omit it.

entranceSide.description: Map edge for the main entrance. Additional entrances can use other edges.

concealedEntrance.description: Adds one secret entrance beyond the visible entrance count. Player-safe exports and viewer details redact this flag to false.

basement.description: Includes a basement within floorCount; it does not add an extra floor.

EncounterMapVerticalConnectionsConfig.description: Basements, dual staircases, ladders and balconies require BUILDING with at least two total floors. Bridges are available for all map types. Balconies require an upper floor above ground, so a building with a basement needs at least three total floors to enable them.

map.description: The snapshot map, present only with `include=map`. Viewers receive the player-safe map.
